chunks: And everything in it that is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri, I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Hasan ibn Matil Al-Daqqaq, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri.

key_terms.أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ: Abi Al-Khattab, a common kunya among Imami scholars
key_terms.الدَّقَّاقِ: Al-Daqqaq, a kunya/nisba meaning 'the small seller' or 'the grocer'
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him

ai.seo_question: How is the narration chain for Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri transmitted in this book?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous attention to *isnad* (transmission chain) by clarifying the specific route through which he received narrations from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri, distinct from other chains. It underscores the scholarly rigor of the Kufan tradition, where precise attribution to authorities like Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ensures the authenticity and reliability of the legal and theological content for the layperson.
